modules.title: 点一个数字，看它变化表达什么兼容承诺
三段数字各自说明什么

items.title: 修订号：通常是修复
items.text: 在遵守 SemVer 的稳定版本中，修订号表示兼容修复；仍要查看发布说明并按项目流程验收。

items.title: 次版本：通常是新增功能
items.text: 在遵守 SemVer 的稳定版本中，次版本表示兼容新增；升级前看新增内容是否影响到你。

items.title: 主版本：可能不兼容
items.text: 在遵守 SemVer 的稳定版本中，主版本表示不兼容变化；升级前读发布说明，改完后按项目流程验收。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: 在 npm 中，^1.2.3 允许主版本 1 内的次版本与修订号更新，不跨到 2.0.0；~1.2.3 只允许 1.2 内的修订号更新。^ 和 ~ 是 npm 的范围语法，不属于 SemVer；其他包管理器可能不同，按对应文档确认。

lessonPractice.title: 示例库 sample-lib 是 ^1.2.3，AI 建议直接改成 2.0.0 并说“版本越新越好”。怎样处理更稳妥？

options.label: 先查 2.0.0 的发布说明，评估不兼容改动对项目的影响再决定
options.feedback: 对。主版本变化可能包含破坏性改动；发布说明列出改动清单，是升级前必须看的材料。

options.label: 直接用最新版本，新版本总是更好的
options.feedback: 版本号新不等于兼容；跨主版本可能让原有代码失效。

options.label: 永远不升级，锁定在所有依赖的最低版本
options.feedback: 长期不升级会积累安全和兼容问题；应按需、按发布说明升级。

en.title: The example library sample-lib is at ^1.2.3, and AI suggests changing it to 2.0.0 because newer is better. What is the more careful approach?

options.label: Check the 2.0.0 release notes for breaking changes and assess the impact before upgrading
options.feedback: Correct. A major version change can include breaking changes; the release notes list them and are required reading before upgrading.

options.label: Always use the newest version because newer is always better
options.feedback: A newer number does not mean compatible; a major bump can invalidate existing code.

options.label: Never upgrade and lock every dependency at its lowest version
options.feedback: Never upgrading accumulates security and compatibility problems; upgrade deliberately based on release notes.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 示例库 sample-lib 当前是 ^1.2.3，请先读 2.0.0 的发布说明，列出会影响本项目的改动，再决定要不要升级。如果决定升级，改完后逐个页面确认没有报错，不要顺手升其他依赖。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: The example library sample-lib is at ^1.2.3. First read the 2.0.0 release notes and list the changes that affect this project, then decide whether to upgrade. If you upgrade, check every page for errors afterward and do not upgrade other dependencies along the way.

learning.assumes: You have seen version numbers on dependencies, or hit errors after an upgrade.
learning.outcome: When a project uses SemVer, you can read the compatibility promise in X.Y.Z and know to check project documentation and actual changes too.

modules.title: Read what each version segment promises

items.title: Patch: usually a fix
items.text: For a stable public API, a patch change promises a compatible fix. Check the project's release notes and run its acceptance checks after upgrading.

items.title: Minor: usually new features
items.text: For a stable public API, a minor release promises compatible additions; check whether the new features affect you.

items.title: Major: possibly incompatible
items.text: For a stable public API, a major release signals incompatible changes; read the release notes before upgrading and verify your project flows afterward.

modules.title: What people often confuse
modules.text: In npm, ^1.2.3 allows minor and patch updates within major version 1, not 2.0.0; ~1.2.3 allows patch updates within 1.2. The ^ and ~ symbols are npm range syntax, not part of SemVer. Other package managers may differ, so check their documentation.

distinctions.label: Date versioning
distinctions.text: Date versions like 2026.09 only mark release time; semantic versioning's three segments each express a change's impact.

distinctions.label: Build number
distinctions.text: A build number only counts builds and says nothing about compatibility; semantic versioning exists to announce compatibility.
